title: domain-factorized Mirror experts
hypothesis: A shared expert bank with one Givens view code per domain can represent the Cartesian product of domain and expert roles using fewer actual bytes than independent domain-expert MLPs.
physical_object: four 16x32x16 GELU experts shared across three domains
mirror_coordinate: domain-specific 2D input/output Givens coordinate, shared across the four expert IDs in a domain
logical_multiplicity: 12 domain x expert functions from 4 physical experts and 3 domain coordinates
controls: one hard-tied four-expert bank shared across domains
shared bank plus per-domain/expert scalar gates
shared bank plus per-domain/expert rank-1 residual
shared bank plus per-domain/expert rank-2 residual
shared bank plus domain-specific Mirror views

task.routing: balanced oracle domain and top-1 expert labels supplied to all methods

teacher_modes.aligned: one shared expert bank under domain-specific Givens input/output views

development.selection_metric: mean held-out MSE across six methods and both teacher modes

fresh.access_condition: At selected LR, aligned Mirror MSE <=1.25x independent and payload <=0.75x independent; otherwise fresh remains sealed.

storage.serialization: torch.save CPU state_dict plus deterministic compact JSON config

success_gate: All three fresh aligned worlds: Mirror MSE <=1.10x independent, payload <=0.65x independent, and at least 10% lower MSE than hard tying at <=10% extra bytes. Compare to domain/expert low-rank controls for Mirror-specific value.
failure_gate: Development gate misses; or >=2 fresh aligned worlds miss quality/storage; or a simple control matches Mirror within 10% MSE at equal/lower bytes in >=2 worlds.
boundaries: aligned teacher deliberately factorizes domain as a shared Givens coordinate
independent teacher measures unrelated domain-expert boundary
